files.content:
# USDC-SOL Escrow Contract

This platform facilitates trustless atomic OTC swaps between USDC (ERC20) and native SOL (wrapped or native network asset).

## Structure
- `Escrow.sol`: Main escrow logic
- `test/Escrow.test.js`: Suite of security validation tests

versions.prompt: Create an escrow smart contract where a maker deposits USDC and a taker can exchange SOL before expiry.
versions.summary: Initial generation of the USDC-SOL escrow system.

audit.summary: The contract is exceptionally well designed. It adheres to Solidity 0.8.20 best practices, uses safe decimal conversions, and successfully mitigates common risks such as reentrancy using the ReentrancyGuard component. Two informational findings were identified regarding event emissions.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Event Emission on Construction
vulnerabilities.description: The constructor establishes crucial escrow state variables like maker, taker, and asset targets, but fails to emit an event informing the blockchain or subgraph indexed layers.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Add a dedicated event `EscrowInitialized` and emit it at the end of the constructor block.

vulnerabilities.title: Use of block.timestamp for Expiry Checks
vulnerabilities.description: The contract relies on block.timestamp to enforce the expiration cutoff of the escrow. Minor timestamp manipulation is possible by validators.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Ensure expiration windows are large enough that minor timestamp drift (+/- 15 seconds) has no material impact on trade execution.
